items.actClause: AN ACT in relation to enacting the "biomass fired exception program" addressing the applicability of a CO2 budget trading program to biomass-fired electric generating facilities that have converted from coal-fired generation
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6709

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act in relation to enacting the "biomass fired
exception program" addressing the applicability of a CO2 budget
trading program to biomass-fired electric generating facilities that
have converted from coal-fired generation

 PURPOSE :

To encourage the development of renewable energy generation through
the conversion of coal-fired electric generating facilities to
biomass-fired facilities.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1: Gives the short title.

Section 2: States the legislature's intent.

Section 3: Provides certain definitions for the purposes of the act.

Section 4: Directs the Commissioner of Environmental Conservation to
promulgate necessary rules and regulations pertaining to treatment of
certain formerly coal-fired electric generating facilities.

Section 5: Sets forth the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

New York State's efforts to encourage converting coal-fired electric
generating facilities to use biomass at Fort Drum's military
installation has helped the upstate economy by creating new
forestry-based jobs which have helped put people back to work while
reducing pollution and CO2 emissions.

Encouraging investment in locally produced renewable energy sources
such as biomass has also helped reduce the state's dependency on
fossil fuels, a key goal of New York State's Regional Greenhouse Gas
Initiative.

The RGGI has encouraged the development of renewable and sustainable
energy sources using a market-based approach that has resulted in a
cleaner environment and economic growth. New York's RGGI program
already encourages the development of new biomass-fired electric
generating facilities. But New York State can continue its leadership
role in promoting environmentally friendly conversions of coal-fired
facilities (boilers, combustion turbines, or combined cycle systems)
by treating the Fort Drum biomass cogenerator plant conversion in the
same manner as it treats the construction of new biomass facilities,
under the RGGI regulations. The result will help encourage other
companies to redevelop coal burning electrical generating facilities
by converting them to biomass facilities while enhancing the financial
viability of Fort Drum's cogenerating facility.

Keeping Fort Drum's cogenerating facility viable will also provide New
York's 10th Mountain Division, the Army's most deployed military unit,
with energy security by providing 100 percent of its electrical needs
on base.

Providing the military installation with its own independent power
grid provides year-round, 24-hour power on base that is less
vulnerable than conventional utility companies to natural disasters or
terrorist attack.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

To be determined

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect within 90 days.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
